```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r}
con = DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "../data/midwest_airbnb_extended.db")
listings     = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "listings") |> tibble::as_tibble()
availability = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "availability_monthly") |> tibble::as_tibble()
reviews      = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "reviews_monthly") |> tibble::as_tibble()
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
```

```{r}
dplyr::glimpse(listings)
```

## Task 1
```{r}
# count listings per host_id and join to listings
host_counts = listings |> 
  dplyr::count(host_id, name = "listing_count")

listings = listings |> 
  dplyr::left_join(host_counts, by = "host_id")

# report how many hosts have more than 10 listings and what percent of chicagos listings these hosts hold
listings |> 
  dplyr::filter(listing_count >= 10) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(
    hosts_10_plus = dplyr::n_distinct(host_id),
    chicago_percent = sum(city == "Chicago") /
                      sum(listings$city == "Chicago") * 100
  )

```

## Task 2
```{r}
# keep entire home/apt that accommodates at least 4, has at least 10 reviews, and reviews 4.8 or better
columbus_value = listings |> 
  dplyr::filter(
    room_type == "Entire home/apt",
    accommodates >= 4,
    number_of_reviews >= 10,
    review_scores_rating >= 4.8
  ) |> # calculate price per person
  dplyr::mutate(
    price_per_person = price / accommodates
  ) |> # group by city and neighbourhood and calculate median price per person
  dplyr::group_by(city, neighbourhood) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(
    median_price_per_person = median(price_per_person, na.rm = TRUE),
    listing_count = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |> # keep columbus neighbourhoods with at least 20 listings
  dplyr::filter(
    listing_count >= 20,
    city == "Columbus"
  ) |> 
  dplyr::arrange(median_price_per_person)

columbus_value

```
## Task 3
```{r}
# calculate median price, reviews per month, and estimated revenue over the last year by city and room type
earnings = listings |> 
  dplyr::group_by(city, room_type) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(
    dplyr::across(
      c(price, reviews_per_month, estimated_revenue_l365d),
      ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# calculate median estimated revenue of Twin Cities entire homes
earnings |> 
  dplyr::filter(
    city == "Twin Cities",
    room_type == "Entire home/apt"
  )
```
## Task 4
```{r}
# Within each city, sort listings by estimated revenue in the last year and mark the top 10%
concentration = listings |> 
  dplyr::group_by(city) |> 
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(estimated_revenue_l365d), .by_group = TRUE) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    top_10 = dplyr::row_number() <= ceiling(0.10 * dplyr::n())
  ) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(
    top_10_revenue = sum(
      estimated_revenue_l365d[top_10],
      na.rm = TRUE
    ), # also calculate total revenue to compare against top 10%
    total_revenue = sum(
      estimated_revenue_l365d,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    percent_revenue = top_10_revenue / total_revenue * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Columbus' total estimated revenue by top 10%
concentration |> 
  dplyr::filter(city == "Columbus")
```
## Task 5
```{r}
# join the october 2026 rows of availability to the entire homes listings
year_ahead = availability |> 
  dplyr::filter(month == "2026-10") |> 
  dplyr::inner_join(
    listings,
    by = "id"
  ) |> 
  dplyr::filter(room_type == "Entire home/apt") |> # formula for mostly taken
  dplyr::mutate(
    mostly_taken = nights_available < 0.5 * nights_in_month
  ) |> # report the city with the lowest share of mostly taken
  dplyr::group_by(city) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(
    share_mostly_taken = mean(mostly_taken, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |> 
  dplyr::arrange(share_mostly_taken)

year_ahead
```
## Task 6
```{r}
# join reviews to listings, keep july 2025 through june 2026
demand = reviews |> 
  dplyr::inner_join(
    listings,
    by = "id"
  ) |> 
  dplyr::filter(
    month >= "2025-07",
    month <= "2026-06"
  ) |> # total the reviews per city and month
  dplyr::group_by(city, month) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(
    total_reviews = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# report the twin cities busiest month and the ratio of its busiest to quietest month
demand |> 
  dplyr::filter(city == "Twin Cities") |> 
  dplyr::summarise(
    busiest_month = month[which.max(total_reviews)],
    busiest_reviews = max(total_reviews),
    quietest_reviews = min(total_reviews),
    ratio = max(total_reviews) / min(total_reviews)
  )
```

## Task 7
```{r}
# create new variable that labels hosts as superhost or other host
superhost_premium = listings |> 
  dplyr::filter(
    room_type == "Entire home/apt",
    host_is_superhost %in% c("t", "f")
  ) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    host_type = dplyr::if_else(
      host_is_superhost == "t",
      "Superhost",
      "Other host"
    )
  ) |> # calculate median price and rating for each group by city
  dplyr::group_by(city, host_type) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(
    median_price = median(price, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_rating = median(review_scores_rating, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |> 
  dplyr::group_by(city) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(
    superhost_median_price = median_price[host_type == "Superhost"],
    other_host_median_price = median_price[host_type == "Other host"],
    premium = superhost_median_price - other_host_median_price,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

superhost_premium
```
## Task 8
```{r}
# calculate the listings that have no rows in availability by city
listings |> 
  dplyr::anti_join(availability, by = "id") |> 
  dplyr::group_by(city) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(
    listings_without_availability = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```
## Task B2
```{r}
# compute the task 1 share for all cities
task1_share = listings |> 
  dplyr::group_by(city) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(
    task1_share = mean(listing_count >= 10) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# compute the task 4 share for all cities
task4_share = listings |> 
  dplyr::group_by(city) |> 
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(estimated_revenue_l365d), .by_group = TRUE) |> 
  dplyr::mutate(
    top_10 = dplyr::row_number() <= ceiling(0.10 * dplyr::n())
  ) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(
    task4_share = sum(
      estimated_revenue_l365d[top_10],
      na.rm = TRUE
    ) /
      sum(estimated_revenue_l365d, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# combine the two results
shares = task1_share |> 
  dplyr::left_join(task4_share, by = "city")

shares
```
